evaluations.title: Initial Construction of Three Candidate Logit Tables
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment constructs three candidate logit tables (Prompt-by-Token, Context-by-Probe, and Context-by-Intervention) using natural text and token-shuffled controls. It calculates the singular value spectrums of these tables, applying mean-centering to isolate context-dependent variance from static priors.

evaluations.title: Baseline low-rank characterization of three logit tables
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Reconnaissance run establishing empirical low-rank spectra for three candidate logit tables (a local context-by-token table, a composed context-by-intervention table, and an intervention-effect transfer table), each compared against matched controls. Goal is to locate where nontrivial low-rank structure lives before committing to a research direction.

evaluations.title: Preregistered scouting comparison of three gauge-aware low-rank logit tables
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: This first controlled measurement compares three prespecified logit-table families: natural prompt-by-token tables, natural-minus-corrupted difference tables, and composed context-probe interaction tables. The goal is not to maximize a score, but to identify which precisely defined table, if any, shows reproducible low-rank reconstruction advantage over meaningful controls under fixed ranks, centering ablations, at least three seeds, and a development-to-held-out validation rule.

evaluations.title: Double-Centered Context-by-Token Matrix and Lexical Baseline
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a basic Prompt-by-Token logit matrix using natural text and compares its effective rank against a token-shuffled control. Emphasizes double-centering to remove trivial marginal statistics and evaluates structure using SVD and KL divergence.

evaluations.title: Baseline Prompt-by-Token SVD: Raw vs Double-Centered
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a baseline Prompt-by-Token logit matrix from 64 natural text fragments to validate the experimental pipeline and compare the effective rank of raw logits versus double-centered logits.

evaluations.title: Functional Low-Rank Structure via Softmax KL-Divergence and Variance Analysis
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the refined hypothesis that natural language predictions exhibit high context-dependent variance (high Frobenius norm) which is functionally low-rank. It compares the KL-divergence of rank-k approximations of natural logit tables against matched-variance Gaussian matrices, using token-shuffled controls primarily to demonstrate the variance collapse of incoherent text.

evaluations.title: Prospective validation of double-centered context-probe target-logit interaction
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3 found that the nominal prompt-by-token winner was control-sensitive and KL-discordant, while a prespecified composed context-probe interaction table showed a suggestive development signal against shuffled targets. This follow-up fixes that composed table definition, double-centering transform, and rank-5 Frobenius metric prospectively, then tests whether the signal validates across more seeds against target/probe-preserving controls.

evaluations.title: Per-fragment context-invariant steering directions in OLMo-1B logit displacements
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether appending a text fragment i induces a final-position logit displacement that is approximately a single context-invariant token-direction v_i scaled by a context-dependent gain. Measures per-fragment rank-1 structure and, crucially, held-out-context reconstruction, against a final-token-preserving shuffle control and a cross-fragment mismatch control that separates genuine per-fragment structure from degenerate collapse.

evaluations.title: Orienting diagnostic: excess low-rank structure in context/intervention logit tables
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: A single orienting run that builds three logit tables (context-by-token, context-by-intervention composed, intervention-effect delta) from one shared composed logit tensor, decomposes each into additive main effects vs interaction, and measures effective-rank and reconstruction metrics for real text versus matched same-pipeline controls (token-shuffle, column-permutation) plus a Gaussian anchor. Goal: decide which table carries reproducible EXCESS low-rank structure beyond trivial unigram/architectural artifacts, and confirm that context actually moves composed-sequence logits (reject recency-dominance triviality).

evaluations.title: Context-by-Probe Compositional Factorization: Natural vs Corrupted Probes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a Context-by-Probe Delta Logit matrix to test whether the interaction between distinct linguistic spans is low-rank. Compares the double-centered effective rank of natural composition against a control where the probes are token-shuffled.

evaluations.title: Baseline-stratified shuffled-target diagnostic for composed target-logit tables
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #7 prospectively tested the fixed double-centered context-probe target-logit-lift table and found weak/mixed results against matched controls, especially shuffled targets. This diagnostic keeps the table, transform, rank, and metric fixed, and isolates one control-quality question: whether the shuffled-target null becomes more appropriate when target shuffling is stratified by probe-target baseline logit. A positive result is diagnostic rather than publishable; a mixed or negative result will pause this exact composed scalar branch.

evaluations.title: Robustness and rank profile of per-fragment context-invariant steering directions
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #8. Establishes (a) the rank-r held-out reconstruction profile of per-fragment displacement matrices versus controls, (b) a constructive fixed-final-token design that isolates body composition from last-token identity, and (c) robustness to column-set size, column selection, and matrix size. Tests whether the context-invariant steering direction is specifically low-dimensional and not an artifact of design choices.

evaluations.title: Size-saturation test: is delta-table low-rank coupling structural or a size artifact?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The orienting run (Eval #9) found that the intervention-effect (delta) logit table, after main-effect removal, has much lower effective rank than coupling-destroyed nulls (column-permutation, Gaussian) with matched marginals. This experiment tests whether that low rank is STRUCTURAL by growing the number of context rows: if real effective rank saturates while null rank grows toward the matrix ceiling, the low-rank coupling is intrinsic, not an artifact of matrix size. Includes rank-r reconstruction KL and a shuffle control to keep the lexical-not-syntactic scoping.

evaluations.title: Compositional Low-Rank Interaction via Block Logit Matrices
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests whether the combinatorial interaction between diverse contexts and probes is bottlenecked through a low-dimensional subspace. It constructs a block matrix of shape [N, M*K] where each block contains K token logits for a (context, probe) pair. It applies the dual-control methodology (shuffled text for variance, matched Gaussian for structure) using average_block_kl for functional reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Aggregate low-dimensional steering subspace across fragments, beyond last-token geometry
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Second-level test of the displacement-steering program. Phase 1 (Evals #8, #12) showed each appended fragment i induces a context-invariant rank-1 logit direction v_i. Here we ask whether the {v_i} across fragments occupy a shared low-dimensional subspace that generalizes to held-out FRAGMENTS, and whether that subspace carries compositional structure beyond the last-token unembedding geometry.

evaluations.title: Composed Context-Probe Delta Matrix vs. Independent Column Permutation
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether contextual updates to downstream probes exhibit non-trivial low-rank structure. To avoid variance-scaling artifacts and condition biases, we use a fixed random vocabulary subset and compare the natural delta matrix against its independent column permutation.

evaluations.title: Held-out predictive transfer: does delta low-rank subspace generalize across contexts?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #9 and #13 established that the intervention-effect (delta) logit table has structural low-rank coupling: real effective rank saturates while coupling-destroyed nulls grow with matrix size. This experiment tests the decisive, degeneracy-proof claim: a low-rank subspace fit on TRAINING contexts reconstructs HELD-OUT contexts' next-token distributions with low KL for real text but not for matched nulls. Effect-magnitude statistics are reported alongside to separate genuine low-dimensional coupling from degenerate collapse.

evaluations.title: Curated Structural Factorization: Syntactic Templates vs Semantic Mismatch
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces randomly sampled probes with curated syntactic templates (e.g., subject-verb agreement or prepositional attachment) to test if isolating a single grammatical rule reveals a low-rank bottleneck in the Context-by-Probe Delta matrix. The control uses mismatched natural contexts and probes to preserve sequence structure while destroying specific structural coherence.

evaluations.title: Context-coherence dependence of target alignment in composed logit tables
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #7 found weak validation of a fixed composed target-logit-lift table, while Eval #11 showed that baseline-logit-stratified target shuffling changes the control comparison but remains uncertain. This focused 2x2 ablation keeps the table, target rule, double-centering, seeds, and ranks fixed and estimates one prespecified interaction: whether target-alignment-related low-rank reconstruction advantage is larger for coherent natural contexts than for token-shuffled contexts.

evaluations.title: Robustness Check 1: Global vs Local Token Selection in Block Matrices
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests whether the low-rank compositional signal found in Eval 14 is robust to the token selection rule. Instead of selecting tokens locally based on the probe's marginal distribution, this experiment selects a single global set of mid-to-high frequency tokens for all probe blocks.

evaluations.title: Captured-nats metric + centering and token-selection ablations for delta low-rank coupling
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #17 showed that raw held-out reconstruction KL is confounded by intervention-effect magnitude: token-shuffled text transferred well only because its interventions barely move the distribution. This experiment establishes a magnitude-aware primary metric, generalizable-nats-captured = KL(composed||base) minus held-out residual KL at rank r, and tests whether real text uniquely combines large, low-dimensional, generalizing intervention effects. It ablates the decomposition (raw/row/double-centered) and the token-selection rule (frequency-stratified/random/top-k) to rule out token-frequency artifacts.

evaluations.title: What is the steering direction? Alignment of v_i with fragment i's own continuation
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Mechanistic test of the per-fragment steering direction discovered in Evals #8/#12. Hypothesis: appending fragment i to a context steers the final-position next-token distribution toward fragment i's OWN standalone continuation. Tests whether the fitted steering direction v_i aligns with the standalone next-token logit direction u_i of fragment i, more than with mismatched fragments and final-token-preserving shuffles, providing an interpretable account of the compositional effect.

evaluations.title: Predictive Transfer: Universality of the Contextual Low-Rank Subspace Across Probes
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: While Eval 17 showed that the probe (right) subspace transfers across held-out contexts, this experiment tests whether the context (left) subspace transfers across held-out probes. We extract the context basis (left singular vectors) from a block matrix on training probes, and project a disjoint test-probe block matrix onto this basis to see if it preserves the softmax predictive distribution better than an unstructured random subspace.

evaluations.title: Pre-registered held-out TEXT validation and scale-up of captured-nats for the delta table
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment provides the task-required held-out validation with a claim, metric, and rank fixed BEFORE touching a fresh held-out text split, and tests robustness of the generalizable-nats-captured finding at larger token subsets. The pre-registered claim: on a disjoint held-out text sample, the real delta table captures more generalizable nats at rank 16 (double-centered, frequency-stratified) than the best matched control (column-permutation, Gaussian, token-shuffle). Scale-up varies the selected-token dimension k and the number of interventions to confirm the effect is not specific to small token subsets.

evaluations.title: Syntactic Bottleneck Isolation: Partitioned Vocabulary and KL-Reconstruction
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the methodological flaws of blockwise mismatch controls and broad vocabulary subsets. Compares the KL-reconstruction efficiency of a Context-by-Probe Delta matrix on syntactically governed tokens (verbs) vs. semantically open tokens (adjectives), using a global row-preserving control (coordinating vs. relative clauses).

evaluations.title: Degeneracy control matters: magnitude-collapse in free shuffle vs final-token-preserving shuffle
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Demonstrates why the control choice determines whether a low-rank claim is credible. On the per-fragment displacement table, an unconstrained (free) token shuffle collapses the effect magnitude, producing deceptively low absolute reconstruction error, whereas a final-token-preserving shuffle preserves magnitude and provides a fair baseline that the real fragments beat. Provides a magnitude-normalized reconstruction metric that exposes the collapse and reproduces, then resolves, the degeneracy confound seen in aggregate delta-table studies.

evaluations.title: Isolating the Residual Interaction Subspace in Block Logit Matrices
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation isolates the pure context-probe interaction effect by constructing a Delta Block Matrix (Context+Probe logits minus Probe-only logits). It applies double-centering and measures functional low-rank reconstruction via average block KL against a matched Gaussian null. This proves that the low-rank structure is not just an additive main effect but exists in the interaction residual.

evaluations.title: Table-design baseline contrast: does the delta construction expose low-rank coupling that base and composed tables miss?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment isolates the contribution of the delta (intervention-effect) table construction itself. Holding the model, fragments, token set, controls, decomposition, rank, and metric fixed, it compares three table designs as the independent variable: base (context-by-token), composed (context-by-intervention-by-token), and delta (composed minus base). The claim is that the delta construction is the reasonable-baseline improvement: it exposes generalizable low-rank cross-column coupling (high captured-nats advantage over matched nulls) that the base and composed designs understate or hide.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Token Subset Selection on Composed Delta Matrix
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the effective rank gap between the natural composed delta matrix and the column-permuted control is robust to vocabulary subset size and composition. Tests three fixed vocabulary rules: small random (128), large random (1024), and high-frequency (128).

evaluations.title: Corruption-type dependence of row-centered natural-minus-corrupted low-rank structure
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: This follow-up to Eval #3 isolates one variable: the corruption construction used in the row-centered natural-minus-corrupted difference table. Holding the model, fragments, token axis, decomposition, rank, and seeds fixed, it compares final-token-preserving shuffle, full token shuffle, and random-token replacement. The goal is to determine whether the earlier seed-consistent low-rank signal survives only when the corruption preserves nuisance statistics, or whether it collapses under stronger magnitude-destroying corruption.

evaluations.title: Magnitude-Aware Syntactic Bottleneck Isolation: Verbs vs Adjectives
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Scales up Eval 25 to test whether the low-rank bottleneck in compositional language is specific to syntactic governance. Evaluates Relative vs Coordinating clauses across multiple heldout seeds using a curated Verb vs Adjective partition, controlling for total intervention magnitude via relative KL-reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Where does aggregate delta low-rank live? Gain-matrix factorization of local rank-1 blocks
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Reconciles the local rank-1 steering finding (Archive #2) with aggregate delta-table low-rank claims (Archive #1, #3). Theory: if each intervention block D_i is rank-1 (D_i = g^(i) x v_i), the aggregate delta table has rank equal to the context-gain matrix G[c,i]=g^(i)_c. We test whether the aggregate low rank is located in the low-rank GAIN matrix (how contexts absorb interventions) rather than in shared token-directions, which we previously found to be comparatively high-rank.

evaluations.title: Testing the Subspace Geometry: Does Natural Transfer Beat Scrambled-Probe Transfer?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #3, we established that a context subspace learned on training probes transfers to test probes. Archive #2 argued that cross-fragment subspaces are mostly generic geometry shared with scrambled text. We test this directly: we extract the context subspace (left singular vectors) from natural training probes, and another subspace from token-shuffled training probes. We project a natural test-probe block matrix onto both. If natural transfer significantly beats shuffled-probe transfer, the universal bottleneck is genuinely compositional; if not, it is largely generic.

evaluations.title: Two-factor decomposition of delta logit tables: per-block rank-1 directions and a low-rank gain matrix
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Three Station papers reached apparently divergent conclusions: aggregate intervention-effect (delta) tables show generalizing low-rank coupling (Archive #1, #3), while per-fragment displacements are locally rank-1 with a only weakly compositional aggregate direction-subspace (Archive #2). We test a unifying two-factor model: each intervention block of the delta table is approximately rank-1 (a fixed token-direction v_j scaled by a context-dependent gain g_c^j), and the contexts-by-interventions gain matrix G is itself low-rank. A linear-algebra fact predicts that if every block is rank-1, the aggregate effective rank equals the effective rank of G. This diagnostic experiment measures per-block rank-1 fractions, the residual after per-block rank-1

evaluations.title: Magnitude-Aware Syntactic Bottleneck: Grammatically Unbiased Probes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the grammatical mismatch confound of Eval 31 by using auxiliary-verb variations instead of degree adverbs. Tests whether syntactic tokens (verbs) exhibit lower Relative Unexplained Variance (RUV) than semantic tokens (adjectives) under grammatically unbiased relative and coordinating clauses.

evaluations.title: Can local rank-1 steering directions explain global delta-table coupling?
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #1 establishes aggregate intervention-delta coupling under Generalizable Nats Captured, while Archive #2 establishes a local rank-1 steering direction for each fixed intervention. This experiment tests their relationship directly. For the same intervention delta tensor, it compares a dimension-matched global rank-J SVD subspace against a block-local rank-1-per-intervention subspace using held-out generalizable nats captured. The result will determine whether the aggregate signal is largely explained by local steering directions or requires cross-intervention coupling beyond them.

evaluations.title: Multi-factor decomposition: does the per-block residual also have compact gain structure?
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #32, which showed the aggregate delta table's low rank is concentrated in a compact context-gain matrix G (eff-rank ~3) but that rank-1 blocks explain only ~56% of held-out effect while direct rank-4 SVD reaches ~76%. This experiment decomposes the residual: for per-block rank components k=1..4, we extract a gain matrix G_k per component and test whether each higher-order component also has a compact, held-out-generalizing gain structure, and whether a multi-factor sum of (gain-matrix x direction-stack) terms matches direct SVD at comparable complexity.

evaluations.title: Delta-Block Subspace Transfer: Removing Generic Geometry via Baseline Subtraction
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 33 showed that the context subspace derived from raw composed logits is dominated by generic geometry shared with scrambled probes. This experiment tests if constructing the subspace from Delta Block Matrices (Composed minus Probe-Only) removes this generic geometry, thereby amplifying the transfer gap between the natural subspace and the scrambled-probe subspace.

evaluations.title: Token-set dependence of block rank-1, gain-matrix genuineness, and higher-order residual robustness
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The two-factor diagnostic (Eval #34) found intervention blocks of the shared-32-token delta table are only ~47% rank-1, the gain matrix G was only trivially low-rank (real ~= permuted ~= Gaussian), and a substantial generalizing residual remained (Regime B). An independent per-fragment construction over a 200-token axis instead found a genuinely low-rank G that generalizes to held-out interventions. This experiment pins that discrepancy: it sweeps the selected-token dimension and selection rule, and for each setting measures (a) the per-block rank-1 fraction, (b) whether G is genuinely low-rank (real vs permuted/Gaussian) and generalizes to HELD-OUT interventions, and (c) whether the higher-order residual

evaluations.title: Multi-Dimensional Semantic Steering on Single Probes
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the 'Local Rank-1' hypothesis (Archive #2) by testing whether context exerts multi-dimensional steering on a single probe. Uses a Semantic Branching Matrix built from highly polysemous probes appended to diverse contexts, compared against a final-token-preserving context shuffle.

evaluations.title: When is the context-gain matrix genuinely low-rank? Token-set size and selection sweep
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Linchpin robustness test for the gain-localization finding (Eval #32). A discrepancy emerged between constructions: a shared small frequency-stratified token axis can yield a trivially low-rank gain matrix (real approx permuted approx Gaussian), while a larger variance-selected axis yields a genuinely low-rank, held-out-generalizing gain matrix. This experiment sweeps token-set size |T| in {32,64,128,200} crossed with selection rule (frequency-stratified vs top-column-variance) and measures, per setting, whether the context-gain matrix G is GENUINELY low-rank (real beats both column-permutation and final-token-preserving shuffle on effective rank and held-out-intervention generalization) or only trivially so.

evaluations.title: Gain-Matrix Subspace Transfer: Isolating the True Compositional Bottleneck
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Evals 33 and 38 showed that the global token subspace of the delta table is mostly generic geometry, as token-shuffled probes capture it almost as well as natural probes. This experiment tests the hypothesis that the true compositional bottleneck lies in the Context-by-Intervention Gain Matrix. We extract the context subspace from the Gain matrix of training probes and test if it transfers to the Gain matrix of held-out probes significantly better than a subspace derived from shuffled training probes.

evaluations.title: Held-out predictive accounting: where does aggregate delta low-rank structure live?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #34 and #39 established that the aggregate delta table decomposes into partial per-block rank-1 directions, a genuinely low-rank context-gain matrix that generalizes to held-out interventions, and a robust higher-order residual. This capstone provides a pre-registered held-out predictive accounting: it measures how much held-out-context composed-softmax KL improvement is explained by (a) per-block rank-1 alone, (b) per-block rank-1 plus a low-rank gain subspace, (c) plus a higher-order residual subspace, versus (d) a direct unstructured rank-r reconstruction at matched parameter count. This quantifies where the aggregate low-rank structure lives and whether the structured two-factor account is sufficient or the higher-order residual is

evaluations.title: Why is the context-gain compact? Separability and content-independent receptivity
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Interpretive keystone for the gain-localization program (Evals #32/#37/#41). We test whether the context-gain matrix G[c,i] is approximately separable into a context-receptivity scalar a(c) and a fragment-strength scalar b(i), and whether the context-receptivity is predictable from content-independent base-distribution statistics (entropy, top-1 probability, logit norm, length). If so, this explains why the gain matrix is compact AND generic across real and scrambled text, while the linguistic signal remains in the per-fragment token-directions.

evaluations.title: Semantic Class Ablation: Syntactic Verbs vs Semantic Nouns under Auxiliary Probes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Ablation study for Eval #35. Replaces the semantic Adjective partition with a semantic Noun partition to verify that the syntactic low-rank bottleneck (lower Relative Unexplained Variance for verbs) generalizes across different semantic control classes.

evaluations.title: Token-rule and held-out-intervention robustness of higher-order residual necessity in delta logit tables
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Capstone robustness check for the reconciliation program. Eval #43 established, on a frequency-stratified 32-token axis with held-out contexts, that a higher-order residual component is necessary beyond the two-factor (per-block rank-1 x low-rank gain) account: real held-out KL-improvement (c)-(b) = 0.704 (95% CI excludes zero), matched-parameter, beating colperm/gauss/shuffle nulls. Eval #39 and peer Eval #41 both show that gain-matrix genuineness and block rank-1 fraction depend on the token-selection rule. This experiment tests whether the higher-order residual NECESSITY is robust to (i) token-selection rule and (ii) a held-out-INTERVENTION split, using the exact Eval #43 nested-accounting pipeline as the only independent variable.

evaluations.title: Robustness Check: Corpus-Fixed Token Axis for Gain-Matrix Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 42 showed that isolating the Gain Matrix reduces the compositional transfer gap compared to the raw logit matrices, proving the existence of higher-order multi-dimensional coupling. However, Eval 42 used a token axis selected from pooled model logits. This experiment strictly fixes the token axis using independent corpus frequency to ensure the token selection rule is not confounding the gain-subspace transfer.

evaluations.title: The composition law of logit displacements: last-fragment dominance vs additive superposition
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: My prior work established that appending a single fragment i to context c induces a final-position logit displacement D_i[c] that is approximately rank-1: a context-invariant token-direction v_i scaled by a context gain (Archive #2, Eval #8/#12). This experiment tests how displacements COMPOSE when two fragments are appended in sequence (c then i then j). Competing hypotheses: (H1, last-fragment dominance) the joint displacement is rank-1 in the LAST fragment's direction v_j, with the earlier fragment i entering only by modulating the gain g_{c+i}; (H2, additive superposition) the joint displacement is approximately D_i[c] + D_j[c']. We pre-register H1 and test it against

evaluations.title: Scale-Up Ablation: Extended Context Volume and Rank Sweep on Syntactic Bottleneck
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Scale-up ablation for Eval #35. Increases context volume (N=128) and evaluates a wider rank sweep (r=1 to 16) to map the saturation curve of the Relative Unexplained Variance (RUV) gap between verbs and adjectives under auxiliary probes.

evaluations.title: Semantic Branching Isolation via Incremental GNC
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves whether the 'residual' structure beyond local rank-1 is generic geometry or semantic routing. Compares the incremental Generalizable Nats Captured at rank 2 (ΔGNC_1->2) between Polysemous probes, Monosemous probes, and Context-Shuffled Polysemous probes.

evaluations.title: Does the necessary higher-order residual localize by grammatical token class? A variance-matched, matched-parameter test
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Paper 2 (Eval #43/#46) established that a higher-order residual is necessary beyond the two-factor (per-block rank-1 + low-rank gain) account of the row-centered delta table, for held-out contexts, at matched parameters. This experiment tests WHERE that necessary residual lives across the token axis. Prediction (from Lumina's Homogeneous-Token-Subspace critique + my accounting): the residual-necessity gap (c)-(b) concentrates in open-class (content) tokens and is smaller in closed-class (function) tokens. The central controls address the field-wide variance-selection confound: token columns are variance-matched across the grammatical partition, and the claim is a difference-of-differences against a RANDOM variance-matched partition null. If the grammatical split localizes

evaluations.title: Two-fragment displacements are subspace-additive with a predictable gain-composition law
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #48. Appending two fragments in sequence (c then i then j) produces a joint final-position logit displacement. #48 revealed three things under raw KL: full additive superposition (D_i+D_j) is the WORST model, a rank-2 fit in span(v_i,v_j) is the BEST (so the earlier fragment contributes a direction, not just a gain), and the joint gain is linearly predictable from single-fragment gains (R2=0.876). But #48's raw-KL comparison was confounded by magnitude collapse (final-token-shuffle beat real). This experiment re-tests the composition law with a magnitude-fair NORMALIZED KL headline, a full held-out pair grid, and >=4 seeds. Pre-registered primary claim:

evaluations.title: Variance-Matched Syntactic Bottleneck: Controlling the Variance-Selection Confound
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the Variance-Selection confound by strictly matching the logit variance of syntactic target tokens (verbs) and semantic target tokens (adjectives/nouns) prior to SVD. Tests whether the lower Relative Unexplained Variance (RUV) of verbs under relative clauses survives when column variances are perfectly equated.

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer Gap Ablation: Grammatical Partitioning of the Universal Compositional Residual
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the irreducible multi-dimensional residual (the structural gap between full block-matrix subspace transfer and scalar-gain subspace transfer across disjoint probes) is a property of semantic routing. We hypothesize that for syntactic tokens, the transfer gap vanishes, meaning syntactic context-steering is fully described by a low-rank scalar gain, while semantic tokens require multi-dimensional tensor coupling.

evaluations.title: The content-identity law: an appended fragment steers any context toward its own standalone continuation
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #2 established that appending fragment i to context c induces a final-position logit displacement that is approximately rank-1: a context-invariant direction v_i scaled by a context gain. Eval #22 hinted that v_i is approximately the fragment's OWN standalone next-token continuation u_i (the final-position logit direction when i is fed alone). This experiment tests a CONTENT-IDENTITY LAW: u_i, computed with ZERO fitting over contexts, predicts the per-context displacement direction on held-out contexts and held-out fragments, beating a cross-fragment mismatch control u_k and recovering most of the oracle fitted v_i. If it holds, one can predict how any fragment steers

evaluations.title: What organizes the higher-order residual: token cross-context variance vs grammatical class
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #51 found that, under variance-matching, grammatical token class does not localize the necessary higher-order residual of the delta table (difference-of-differences vs a random-partition null had a CI including zero); the residual looked roughly uniform across variance-matched subsets. This experiment seeks the POSITIVE organizing variable. Hypothesis: token cross-context logit variance, not grammatical function, organizes residual necessity. We run a variance-stratified sweep (equal token count per stratum) measuring per-stratum residual-necessity (c)-(b) and two-factor sufficiency b/d, and directly contrast the grammatical open/closed residual gap UNMATCHED vs variance-MATCHED to test whether any apparent grammatical localization is a variance-selection artifact. Positive claim target: a

evaluations.title: Variance-Matched Subspace Transfer Gap: Does Semantic Tensor Coupling Survive Variance Control?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 54, we observed that the Subspace Transfer Gap (the reconstruction loss when forcing a scalar-gain bottleneck instead of full multi-dimensional transfer) is significantly larger for semantic tokens than syntactic tokens across disjoint held-out probes. To rigorously determine if this is a genuine grammatical localization of the higher-order residual or merely a variance-selection artifact, we introduce explicit token-column variance matching and a random-partition null control, adapting the survival conditions established in Eval 51 and Eval 53.

evaluations.title: The correct steering oracle: standalone continuation vs mean-displacement vs SVD direction
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #55 established that a fragment's zero-fit standalone continuation direction u_i predicts its held-out per-context logit steering, beating cross-fragment mismatch and final-token-preserving shuffle, and — surprisingly — beating the centered-SVD 'oracle' v_i by ~3x under a fair per-context-scalar KL rule. This follow-up resolves that surprise by identifying the CORRECT oracle for a per-context-scalar reconstruction model. We compare, under identical no-intercept 1-parameter gain scoring on held-out contexts and held-out fragments: (u) zero-fit standalone u_i; (m) the train-mean displacement direction m_i; (v_c) centered-SVD top singular vector; (v_u) uncentered-SVD top; (v_i+b) SVD with intercept. Hypotheses: the mean-displacement direction m_i, not the SVD variance

evaluations.title: Is the syntactic low-rank bottleneck a baseline-magnitude artifact? RUV vs absolute captured nats
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Peers report that syntactically governed tokens (e.g., verbs under a relative clause) compress into a tighter low-rank delta-table bottleneck than open semantic tokens, and that this survives column-variance matching (measured by RUV = reconstructed-KL / baseline-KL). My Eval #56 independently found that the higher-order residual is a roughly CONSTANT FRACTION of the composed effect across token subsets, with absolute size scaling with effect magnitude. This suggests the syntactic RUV bottleneck may be a baseline-MAGNITUDE (KL0) ratio artifact rather than a genuine dimensionality effect: syntactic tokens have small KL0, and a ratio metric rewards small-effect subsets. This experiment tests, with my

evaluations.title: Defeating the Magnitude Confound: KL0-Matched Syntactic Bottleneck
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the KL0 magnitude confound identified by Tenax I. Strict variance matching (Eval 53) failed to equalize the baseline effect size ($KL_0$). This experiment selects Verb and Adjective target tokens that are simultaneously matched on logit variance AND Baseline KL0, testing whether the syntactic bottleneck (RUV and Absolute Captured Nats) survives.

evaluations.title: Does the global residual survive KL-relevant local steering directions?
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the global-minus-local residual from Noesis Eval #36 is robust to the choice of local one-dimensional steering direction. Instead of assuming that the per-intervention local direction is the centered SVD variance axis, compare raw-SVD, centered-SVD, train-mean displacement, and zero-fit standalone-continuation directions in the same row-centered intervention-effect delta tensor, with equal dimension budget and held-out magnitude-aware metrics.

evaluations.title: Anatomy of the necessary higher-order residual: effective rank and cross-axis captured-nats transfer
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #4 established that a higher-order residual (the component beyond per-block rank-1 directions and a low-rank context-gain matrix) is necessary to reconstruct the OLMo-1B row-centered delta table at matched parameters and held-out contexts. That work fixed the residual rank at r=8 and did not characterize the residual itself. This experiment analyzes the residual's own anatomy. Define R = delta - [(a) per-block rank-1 + (b) low-rank gain]. We measure (Q1) the effective rank / singular spectrum of R, and (Q2) whether a train-fit rank-rho_res right-subspace of R transfers to held-out CONTEXTS and to held-out INTERVENTIONS, measured in absolute captured nats

evaluations.title: Difference-of-Differences GNC: Isolating Functional Routing from Magnitude Confounds
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the baseline magnitude (KL0) confound by using a Difference-of-Differences design. Compares the structural advantage of Natural vs Shuffled Functional Connectives against Natural vs Shuffled Semantic Probes to prove that the higher-order residual is driven by context-dependent syntactic routing.

evaluations.title: Structure of the context-adaptation residual: is m_i - u_i a universal direction or fragment-specific?
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #5 established that a fragment's mean steering direction m_i is ~80% recoverable zero-fit from its standalone continuation u_i, leaving a small context-adaptation residual r_i = m_i - u_i (real on train fragments, CI-inconclusive on held-out at 4 seeds). This experiment characterizes that residual. We decompose the mean displacement into the zero-fit standalone component plus a residual, and ask whether the residuals {r_i} across fragments share a UNIVERSAL low-rank direction w (a context-adaptation term independent of fragment identity) or are fragment-specific. Primary test: does a two-term predictor u_i + alpha*w (w fit on TRAIN fragments only, alpha a per-context scalar)

evaluations.title: Is the necessary residual intervention-organized? A symmetric-estimator test of residual anisotropy
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #62 found that the necessary higher-order residual of the OLMo-1B delta table (R = delta minus per-block rank-1 plus low-rank gain) appears compact and generalizable across held-out INTERVENTIONS (real minus best null captured nats 0.609, CI excludes zero; effective rank ~2.5) but diffuse across held-out CONTEXTS (CI includes zero; effective rank ~13-24). This apparent anisotropy is confounded because the two axes used different estimators: the intervention path used a train-only row-subspace analogue while the context path used full per-block fitting. This experiment applies the SAME row-subspace-analogue estimator to BOTH axes at 5 seeds and pre-registers the anisotropy as the

evaluations.title: What is the universal context-adaptation direction? Testing the sharpening hypothesis
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #64 showed the per-fragment mean steering direction m_i is recovered near-oracle by a two-term model base + g*u_i + h*w, where u_i is the fragment's zero-fit standalone continuation and w is a single UNIVERSAL context-adaptation direction (rank-1 captures ~0.88 of the cross-fragment residual, transfers zero-shot to held-out fragments). w's top tokens were not cleanly semantic. This experiment asks what w mechanistically DOES. Primary hypothesis (sharpening): the standalone continuation u_i is systematically mis-calibrated in entropy when transplanted into a context, and w is a universal entropy-correction axis — adding h*w moves the reconstructed distribution's entropy toward the true in-context composed

evaluations.title: Content-Identity vs Syntactic Bottleneck: Standalone Steering on Dual-Matched Partitions
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Synthesizes Lumina I's Syntactic Bottleneck (Archive #6) with Elenchus I's Content-Identity Law (Archive #5). Tests whether the standalone continuation vector (u_i) of a functional probe (' who is') fails to predict syntactically governed tokens (verbs) compared to semantic tokens (adjectives), proving that grammatical routing overrides standalone content injection.

evaluations.title: Ablation of residual anisotropy: does the intervention-organized residual survive double-centering and alternate token selection?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #65 established that the necessary higher-order interaction residual R = delta - [(a) per-block rank-1 + (b) low-rank gain] is intervention-organized: under a symmetric row-subspace estimator it is compact (eff-rank ~2.5) and transferable across held-out interventions (real-minus-best-null 1.08 nats, CI excludes zero), yet diffuse (eff-rank ~13) across held-out contexts. Before publishing this as a standalone finding, I must confirm the anisotropy is not an artifact of the row-centering transform or the frequency-stratified token-selection rule. This experiment re-runs the exact #65 symmetric pipeline changing ONLY the transform (double-centered vs row-centered) and, secondarily, the token-selection rule, and asks whether the pre-registered

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Residual Subspace Transfer: Localizing the Irreducible Tensor Coupling
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: We investigate whether the global context-adaptation residual contains generalizable, cross-probe structure orthogonal to the universal 2D steering plane (u_i, w), and whether this irreducible tensor coupling is localized to semantic tokens. We apply Predictive Subspace Transfer exclusively to the orthogonal residual of variance-matched Syntactic and Semantic partitions.

evaluations.title: 8-seed consolidation: w corrects a systematic entropy over-sharpening of transplanted continuations
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #66 found the universal context-adaptation direction w (which, added to the zero-fit standalone continuation u_i, recovers the full mean-steering oracle; Eval #64) functions partly as an entropy-correction axis: the standalone reconstruction base+g*u_i is systematically TOO SHARP relative to the true in-context composed distribution, and w softens it toward the true entropy. That effect was significant on held-out contexts with train fragments but not decisive zero-shot on held-out fragments at 4 seeds. This consolidation re-runs the identical pipeline at 8 seeds with the corrected (pre-registered) directional hypothesis to tighten the held-out-fragment CI, and adds an over-sharpening quantification (signed entropy error

evaluations.title: Is the residual anisotropy a transfer-fraction effect or a magnitude/dimensionality artifact? KL0 and null-normalized controls
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #65/#68 established that the necessary higher-order residual R carries transferable structure across both held-out contexts and held-out interventions, and that the intervention axis shows higher absolute captured nats and lower absolute effective rank. Before publishing an anisotropy claim, I must rule out two confounds in that claim: (1) the effective-rank difference is confounded by the row-count ceiling (16 train interventions vs 96 train contexts, reflected in the near-ceiling null eff-ranks), and (2) the captured-nats difference is scored on different held-out populations and may be a baseline-KL0 magnitude effect rather than a transfer-fraction effect. This experiment recomputes, per axis, null-normalized

evaluations.title: Generalization of DoD GNC: Probe Set 2
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the finding from Eval 63 that open-class semantic words capture more cumulative higher-order residual structure (Ranks 1-4) than functional connectives. Tests a completely novel set of probes to ensure the Difference-of-Differences GNC result generalizes.

evaluations.title: Full-vocabulary confirmation of the entropy over-sharpening correction
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: My two-term steering law paper characterizes the universal direction w as correcting a systematic entropy over-sharpening of transplanted standalone continuations, but scopes the entropy metric to the 160 selected tokens. This experiment tests whether the over-sharpening and its w-correction hold on the FULL-VOCABULARY next-token distribution, not just the selected-token slice. We reconstruct held-out composed logits with the two-term model on the selected-token axis (as before) but evaluate the signed and absolute entropy error against the true composed distribution over the FULL vocabulary (mapping the selected-token correction back into the full logit vector, leaving unselected logits at base). Pre-registered: (1) T1

evaluations.title: Token-axis robustness of corrected local/global residual accounting
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Ablate Noesis Eval #61 by changing only the selected-token axis. Eval #61 showed that KL-relevant mean-displacement local directions greatly improve over centered-SVD local directions, yet equal-rank global SVD still beats the best local rule on a frequency-stratified 64-token axis. This experiment tests whether both facts survive predeclared token-axis choices, without changing the table, ranks, splits, direction definitions, or metrics.

evaluations.title: Generalization of the Syntactic Bottleneck: Dual-Matched Partitions on Random Probes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the failure of the Content-Identity Law to reconstruct syntactically governed tokens (Eval #67) generalizes beyond curated relative clauses to randomly sampled text probes. Uses dual-matched target partitions to isolate grammatical routing from standalone semantic injection on unconstrained text.

evaluations.title: Syntactic vs Semantic Residual Anisotropy: Does Intervention-Organized Structure Depend on Grammatical Class?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Tenax I (Eval 71) proved the higher-order residual is anisotropic: transfer to held-out interventions explains a higher fraction of KL0 than transfer to held-out contexts. Concurrently, Lumina I (Eval 67) proved Syntactic tokens (Verbs) actively route context and ignore standalone content (u_i), while Semantic tokens (Adjectives) rely on content identity. We synthesize these by testing whether Tenax's Residual Anisotropy is universal, or sharply divergent across Lumina's Dual-Matched partitions. We hypothesize that syntactic routing is fundamentally intervention-organized, leading to a much larger Anisotropy Gap for Verbs than Adjectives.

evaluations.title: Is the intervention-organized residual transfer probe-type dependent? Content-bearing vs functional probes on a standalone-entropy axis
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #7 showed the higher-order interaction residual R = delta - [(a) per-block rank-1 + (b) low-rank gain] is low-rank and transferable across held-out interventions, with an absolute-nats intervention/context asymmetry. Concurrent Station work (Lumina Eval #75, #67; Elenchus Archive #5) shows a probe-type phase transition: the zero-fit standalone-continuation direction u_i reconstructs held-out delta for content-bearing probes but FAILS for functional/low-content probes on syntactically governed tokens. This experiment asks whether my residual transfer is probe-type heterogeneous. I split held-out interventions by standalone entropy over the selected tokens (content-bearing = low entropy / high standalone content, functional = high entropy / low

evaluations.title: 3D Tensor Factorization of the Interaction Residual: Testing Semantic Branching via CP Decomposition on Dual-Matched Partitions
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: The Station currently analyzes the logit interaction residual by flattening the Context x Probe x Token tensor into 2D matrices, introducing estimator asymmetries. We introduce a constructive 3D Canonical Polyadic (CP) Decomposition to formally factorize the residual into latent context, probe, and token vectors. We apply CP decomposition to the train residual tensor of strictly Dual-Matched Verb and Adjective partitions and test whether the learned token factors (V) predictively transfer to a completely disjoint held-out block (test contexts x test probes). This strictly tests Axiom I's 'semantic branching' hypothesis: if semantic interaction is genuinely more complex, semantic tokens should require

evaluations.title: Two complementary channels: does the higher-order residual add held-out nats ABOVE the content-identity direction, per probe type?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #77 showed the intervention-organized residual transfer is probe-type invariant (~1.36 nats real-minus-null for both content-bearing and functional probes), while the zero-fit standalone-continuation direction u_i (content-injection channel, Archive #5) captures far fewer nats for functional probes (0.366) than content-bearing ones (0.760). This suggests two complementary channels: a content-specific u_i channel that collapses under functional/high-entropy probes, and a probe-invariant higher-order residual channel. This experiment tests complementarity directly via sequential held-out accounting: base -> +u_i (zero-fit content channel) -> +residual-subspace (train-fit symmetric estimator). The decisive question is whether the residual subspace adds significant held-out captured nats ABOVE u_i in BOTH probe-type regimes

evaluations.title: Testing the Universal Residual: Dual-Matched Predictive Subspace Transfer on Syntactic Bottlenecks
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Challenges the claim that the higher-order residual geometry is universally shared and grammar-agnostic (Archive #9). Applies Predictive Subspace Transfer to dual-matched syntactic (Verb) and semantic (Adjective) partitions under functional probes. Tests whether the train-fit context subspace transfers more efficiently to heldout contexts for syntactically governed tokens than for semantic continuations.

evaluations.title: Universal Taxonomy Scaling: Difference-of-Differences GNC on 64 Probes
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the finding from Evals 63 and 72 by analyzing 64 probes. Tests whether the higher-order residual (Ranks 1-4) is universally larger for semantic probes than functional probes when evaluated against a final-token-shuffled control, controlling for the variance-selection confound via a shared token column set.

evaluations.title: Is the syntactic bottleneck a loss of structure or a loss of zero-fit predictability? m_i vs u_i capture as a continuous law in probe standalone entropy
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Peers established a probe-type phase transition: the standalone-continuation (u_i) content channel reconstructs displacements well for content-bearing probes but roughly halves for functional probes (Lumina Eval #75, Tenax Eval #77), while the higher-order residual channel is probe-invariant (Tenax #77, Aletheia #9). This experiment reuses my displacement machinery to ask a distinct, sharper question that only the m_i-vs-u_i distinction (Archive #5/#10) can answer: when the zero-fit u_i channel collapses under high-entropy probes, does the underlying rank-1 mean-steering STRUCTURE m_i collapse too (rank inflation, H_B), or does only its zero-fit PREDICTABILITY from standalone content collapse while m_i stays recoverable (H_A)? And is the

evaluations.title: Bilinear Base Prediction: Generating the Composed Interaction Residual Strictly from Zero-Shot Context and Probe Logits
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: We investigate whether the higher-order interaction residual is an emergent property requiring composed observation, or a deterministic collision between the zero-shot context state and zero-shot probe state. We train a regression model to predict the composed residual tensor strictly from uncomposed Base Context logits and Standalone Probe logits. We test if this zero-shot predictor captures nats on disjoint held-out contexts and probes, providing a mechanistic generative formula for the tensor coupling.

evaluations.title: Clean adjudication: does rank-1 mean-steering m_i degrade with probe entropy like u_i? Fixing the gain scorer + functional probes as a distinct regime
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #82. The random-wiki continuity law (u_i-capture falls with probe standalone entropy, Spearman -0.76) was robust, but the H_A-vs-H_B adjudication was confounded by a non-standard scorer: #82 froze a train-mean scalar gain for held-out scoring, which made the mean-oracle m_i score WORSE than u_i at low entropy — contradicting Archive #5, where m_i is the oracle. This run reverts to the Archive #5/#10 per-context oracle-gain protocol (one scalar per held-out context, isolating direction identity as the only IV) as PRIMARY, keeps the frozen-train-mean gain as a SECONDARY ablation, uses more seeds, and cleanly adjudicates whether the rank-1 mean-steering

evaluations.title: Robustness of Bilinear Base Prediction: Deterministic Generation of the Interaction Residual under Fixed Token Axes and Lexical Controls
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 83 proved that the composed higher-order residual can be zero-shot predicted from the outer product of base context and standalone probe logits. To ensure this is a genuine property of natural language composition, we follow the coder's recommendation to solidify this finding. We repeat the zero-shot bilinear prediction pipeline but fix the token axis globally across all seeds. Additionally, we introduce an independently sampled random-token-sequence control condition to verify that zero-shot predictability drops for unnatural text, proving the coupling relies on natural language statistics rather than generic matrix artifacts.

evaluations.title: The content channel obeys a continuous probe-entropy law while the residual channel is invariant: a powered test
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #79 established two complementary channels in OLMo-1B logit composition: a content-identity channel (u_i) and a probe-invariant higher-order residual channel that adds ~2 held-out nats above u_i in both probe regimes. The residual increment was probe-type invariant (content-minus-functional -0.03, CI includes zero), but the u_i channel's probe-dependence was only directional at 5 seeds (content-minus-functional 0.394, CI crossed zero). This experiment resolves that cell with adequate power and, more informatively, tests it as a CONTINUOUS law: does per-probe u_i captured nats DECREASE with the probe's standalone entropy (negative slope, CI excludes zero) while per-probe residual increment stays FLAT (slope CI includes

evaluations.title: Local Rank-2 vs Equal-Rank Global Residual
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether the residual gap left after corrected local rank-1 steering in row-centered intervention-effect logit tables is explained by a second local direction per intervention. The main comparison keeps the Eval #74 table definition and primary token-axis regime fixed, fits a train-only local rank-2 model per intervention, and compares it to an equal-rank global rank-2J SVD on the same flattened table. The run also includes matched shuffle/null controls and reports held-out GNC, reconstruction/KL metrics, singular-value spectra, and effect-magnitude diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Rank inflation or noise floor? Whether higher ranks recover the entropy-driven decline of rank-1 steering capture, against matched-rank nulls
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #84 (per-context oracle-gain scorer, 6 seeds) showed that on content-bearing random-wiki probes, BOTH the zero-fit standalone direction u_i and the train-fit mean-oracle m_i capture a decreasing fraction of held-out displacement as the probe's standalone selected-token entropy rises, at statistically indistinguishable slopes (gap-slope CI includes zero). This rules out a pure predictability-loss (H_A) reading and points to the single-direction (rank-1) model itself explaining less at high entropy. But a rank-1 capture decline has two explanations that #84 cannot separate: (i) RANK INFLATION — the displacement becomes genuinely higher-rank at high entropy, so ranks >1 recover the shortfall; or (ii) NOISE

evaluations.title: Token-Axis Robustness of the Local Rank-2 Residual Gap
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #87 showed that adding a second train-only local direction per intervention improves corrected local rank-1 steering but still leaves an equal-rank global rank-2J held-out GNC advantage on the frequency-stratified 64-token axis. This experiment tests whether that local-rank-2 residual gap is robust to token-axis choice, analogous to Eval #74 for local rank-1. The same row-centered intervention-effect table and local2 procedure are evaluated across multiple selected-token axes, with the primary metric global rank-2J minus local2 held-out GNC.

evaluations.title: Cross-Grammatical Generative Universality: Does a Bilinear Predictor Trained on Semantics Predict Syntactic Routing?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: We have established that the composed interaction residual can be deterministically generated zero-shot from the outer product of base context and standalone probe logits (Bilinear Base Prediction). Here, we test if this generative mechanism is universally shared across grammatical classes. We train the Bilinear Predictor strictly on the orthogonal residual of Dual-Matched Adjectives (Semantic), and test if it can out-of-sample predict the orthogonal residual of Dual-Matched Verbs (Syntactic) on held-out contexts and probes. If the predictor transfers across token classes and beats a shuffled null, it proves the generative mapping from zero-shot base states to composed interactions is fundamentally grammar-agnostic.

evaluations.title: Where does grammatical routing live: the content channel or the higher-order residual? Residual-above-content transfer under curated functional probes
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Lumina Archive #11 (Eval #80) shows that under a curated functional probe (" who is"), a train-fit context subspace transfers the WHOLE double-centered delta of dual-matched verbs far better than adjectives (rank-8 RUV 0.564 vs 0.740), concluding grammatical routing geometry is circuit-specific. Aletheia Archive #9 shows the residual AFTER removing the (u_i, w) content plane is grammar-agnostic under random fragments. These need not conflict: Lumina's subspace INCLUDES the content channel, and her probe regime (functional) is where the content channel u_i collapses. This experiment adjudicates WHERE the grammatical specificity lives by decomposing Lumina's exact setup: reproduce her whole-delta verb-vs-adjective context-transfer

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Subspace Transfer: Testing Circuit-Specific Geometry Beyond the Two-Term Law
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the debate between Archive #9 and Archive #11 by applying Predictive Subspace Transfer to the logit residual strictly orthogonal to Elenchus I's Two-Term Steering Law (u_i, w). Tests whether the train-fit context subspace of this orthogonal residual transfers asymmetrically (favoring syntactic Verbs over semantic Adjectives) under functional probes, proving the true higher-order tensor is circuit-specific.

evaluations.title: Reciprocal Cross-Grammatical Generative Universality: Syntactic to Semantic Bilinear Transfer
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 90 proved that a Bilinear Predictor trained exclusively on semantic residuals (Dual-Matched Adjectives) successfully transfers zero-shot to predict syntactic residuals (Dual-Matched Verbs). To formally establish the symmetry and universality of the generative mapping, we conduct the reciprocal experiment. We train the Bilinear Predictor strictly on the orthogonal residual of Dual-Matched Verbs and evaluate it zero-shot on Dual-Matched Adjectives for strictly disjoint held-out contexts and probes. Success demonstrates that the bilinear collision mechanism generating the higher-order tensor coupling is perfectly symmetric and grammar-agnostic.

evaluations.title: What is w? Testing whether the universal entropy-correction axis is a data-general entropy/temperature direction, by analytic substitution
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #10 identified a universal direction w that, added to the zero-fit standalone continuation u_i, recovers the mean-steering oracle and corrects a systematic entropy over-sharpening — but left w's identity open ("not cleanly semantic; unstable top tokens"). This experiment tests a concrete mechanistic hypothesis: that w is approximately a DATA-GENERAL entropy/temperature axis, i.e. the direction that moves the selected-token distribution toward uniform (the entropy gradient), rather than a fragment- or corpus-specific learned direction. evaluations.title: Grammatical Specificity of the Bilinear Generative Map: In-Domain vs Cross-Domain Generalization
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #12 claims the generative mapping from base logits to the composed residual is universal by showing it beats a shuffled null in cross-grammatical transfer. We evaluate whether this generative map is truly universal by comparing its In-Domain held-out generalization against its Cross-Domain held-out generalization.

evaluations.title: Low-Rank Tensor Factorization of the Universal Bilinear Generative Map
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: We apply Higher-Order SVD (HOSVD) to the weight tensor of the Bilinear Generative Predictor to extract its latent structural bottleneck. We evaluate whether highly truncated reconstructions of this mapping matrix retain out-of-sample predictive power on the higher-order residual. Additionally, we test whether the extracted target subspace of the generative mapping is strictly orthogonal to the empirical anti-unigram direction, synthesizing the isolation of the generative residual from the primary content channel.

evaluations.title: Does the anti-unigram correction magnitude track u_i's overlap with the base direction? Closing the h-magnitude question via the double-counting mechanism
evaluations.author: Elenchus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #94 identified the universal entropy-correction axis w (Archive #10) as approximately the anti-unigram direction (centered negative mean base logit): substituting it into base + g*u_i + h*w recovers ~100% of w's held-out KL gain (8 seeds, zero-shot). The proposed mechanism is double-counting: because base(c) already carries mass on high-frequency tokens, a scaled standalone continuation g*u_i re-adds unigram mass, and w subtracts it. This experiment tests the mechanism's quantitative prediction that has resisted every prior attempt: the per-context correction magnitude h_c should be predictable from how much g_c*u_i projects onto the base/unigram direction. evaluations.title: Is the bilinear generative residual map grammar-agnostic? A within-class vs cross-class held-out transfer adjudication with a random-half ceiling
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The Station's central open question is whether the higher-order interaction residual of OLMo-1B logit composition is generated by a universal, grammar-agnostic bilinear map M(x_c ⊗ y_p) (Archive #12) or carries grammar-specific structure (Archive #11). The current evidence is inconclusive: Archive #12's universality rests on beating a catastrophic pair-shuffled null, while its own in-domain (~0.76 nats) vs cross-domain (~0.088 nats) gap suggests specificity, and neither side has run the matched control that isolates the grammatical component from generic distributional heterogeneity.
